B7.name: B7
B7.note: Barre-free B7 voicing matching the teaching prose: index(1) on G-string 2nd fret, middle(2) on D-string 1st fret, ring(3) on A-string 2nd fret, pinky(4) on high-e 2nd fret. Spelling verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js as B D# F# A (root, 3rd, 5th, b7).

exercises.name: Make the B7 shape
exercises.purpose: Land the turnaround chord that completes the 12-bar.

params.fingers: index(1) on G-string 2nd fret, middle(2) on D-string 1st fret, ring(3) on A-string 2nd fret, pinky(4) on high-e 2nd fret
params.strings_played: A, D, G, B, high e (low E stays quiet)

exercises.coaching: B7 is the one that turns the blues around. Four fingers, all close together: index on the G string second fret, middle on the D string first fret, ring on the A string second fret, pinky on the high e second fret. Low E stays quiet. It looks busy but the fingers barely move — that cluster IS the sound.

exercises.name: The turnaround walk
exercises.purpose: Practice E7 to A7 to B7 — the classic blues turnaround.

params.cue: one chord per 4 beats, change on the downbeat

exercises.coaching: Walk the turnaround: E7, A7, B7 — one per four beats. Slow it right down so every change lands on the click. B7 is the tension that wants to resolve back to E7. That pull is the whole story of the blues.

exercises.name: Your first 12-bar blues
exercises.purpose: Play the full 12-bar form top to bottom.

params.cue: one chord per bar, change on bar 1; bars 9-12 are the turnaround

exercises.coaching: Here it is — the 12-bar. E7 for four bars, A7 for two, back to E7 for two, then the turnaround: B7, A7, E7, B7. One chord per bar, on the click. Slow is fine. You are playing the form that underpins a century of music. Loop it. That is the blues.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: The payoff lesson. Three chords — E7, A7, B7 — and you can play a full 12-bar blues. This is the form behind a hundred years of music.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: B7 is the turnaround chord: index on G second fret, middle on D first, ring on A second, pinky on high e second. Low E quiet. The cluster of fingers barely moves — that is the sound.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Walk the turnaround: E7, A7, B7, one per four beats, slow. B7 is the tension that wants to fall back to E7. That pull is the whole story.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: The 12-bar: E7 four bars, A7 two, E7 two, then B7-A7-E7-B7. One chord per bar, on the click. Slow is fine. Loop it. That is the blues.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can play the 12-bar without stopping, you have the backbone of the entire style. Loop it every practice — it never gets old.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: E7, A7, B7 — a full 12-bar blues in your hands. That is the Blues style pack. Play it with the shuffle, play it with feeling, and you are a blues player.
